node.label: Mass and capacity are attributes

node.label: Volume uses cubic units
node.description: Volume is measured with cubic units because it fills three-dimensional space.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Volume layers build from base area
node.description: Prism volume can be seen as layers of base area stacked through height.

node.label: Prism volume is base area times height

node.label: Surface area uses exposed faces

node.label: Nets show all faces
node.description: A net can show every face of a prism so the face areas can be added.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Surface area is area not volume
node.description: Surface area measures exposed two-dimensional faces, not the space inside the solid.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Hidden faces are not exposed
node.description: Internal or shared faces are not counted in the exposed surface area of a composite solid.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Volume units are cubed
node.description: Volume units are cubic units because three dimensions are multiplied.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Volume surface area confusion
node.description: Learner confuses the space inside a solid with the area of its outside faces.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Count visible cubes only
node.description: Learner counts only visible unit cubes and ignores hidden cubes in a prism arrangement.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Use area formula for volume
node.description: Learner uses a two-dimensional area formula when a three-dimensional volume formula is required.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Count hidden faces in surface area
node.description: Learner includes internal shared faces when calculating exposed surface area of a composite solid.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mass capacity confusion
node.description: Learner confuses how heavy an object is with how much a container can hold.

edge.rationale: Mass comparison is a core mass-measurement context.
Capacity comparison is a core capacity-measurement context.
Reading scales is central to measuring mass and capacity with instruments.
Estimating supports unit choice and reasonableness in mass and capacity contexts.
Converting units is common in later mass and capacity contexts.
Unit cubes are the foundational unit for volume of prisms.
Volume as space filled is core conceptual understanding for prisms.
Counting cubic units directly practises volume measurement.
Layer reasoning connects unit cubes to prism volume formulas.
Rectangular prism formula is central to prism volume work.
Base-area-times-height generalises rectangular prism volume to other prisms.
Composite prism volume extends prism volume to decomposed solids.
Capacity-volume links connect prism volume to filled containers.
Nets show all faces used in surface-area calculations.
Surface area is calculated by adding face areas.
Rectangular prism surface area is a central surface-area case.
Triangular prism surface area extends face-area reasoning to triangular faces.
Composite surface area requires identifying exposed faces across combined solids.
Contextual surface-area problems apply face-area reasoning to materials and coverings.
Context problems apply prism volume and capacity relationships.
Missing-dimension problems extend volume formulas into inverse reasoning.
Comparing mass in contexts depends on recognising mass units and the mass attribute.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares visual size instead of mass or chooses capacity units.

edge.rationale: Capacity contexts depend on recognising the capacity attribute and suitable capacity units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses mass or length units for a container's capacity.

edge.rationale: Reading measurement scales requires familiarity with standard measurement units and marked intervals.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads marks as counts rather than values on a scale.

edge.rationale: Estimating mass and capacity requires familiar unit benchmarks.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives implausible estimates or inappropriate units.

edge.rationale: Contextual mass and capacity conversions require converting between related metric units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner changes unit labels without scaling quantities.

edge.rationale: Unit cubes extend equal square-unit area reasoning into three dimensions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats cubic units as flat squares rather than 3D units.

edge.rationale: Understanding volume as filled space is supported by building with unit cubes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts surfaces instead of the space occupied by the object.

edge.rationale: Counting cubic units requires knowing that unit cubes are the repeated volume unit.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts only visible cubes or counts faces instead of cubes.

edge.rationale: Layer reasoning builds from structured counting of cubic units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot infer hidden layers or relate a layer to base area.

edge.rationale: The rectangular prism formula generalises length-by-width layers stacked by height.
edge.failure_signal: Learner multiplies two dimensions only or cannot explain why height is included.

edge.rationale: Base-area-times-height generalises rectangular prism volume to other prism bases.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify a base area or prism height.

edge.rationale: Composite prism volume requires decomposing into prisms and calculating each part's volume.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds surface areas or external dimensions instead of part volumes.

edge.rationale: Relating capacity and volume requires familiarity with capacity units and container contexts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats litres and cubic units as unrelated labels.

edge.rationale: Nets of prisms require identifying faces whose areas can be calculated.
edge.failure_signal: Learner draws a net but cannot connect faces to area calculations.

edge.rationale: Finding face areas depends on identifying all faces of the prism, often through a net.
edge.failure_signal: Learner misses faces or calculates only one face area.

edge.rationale: Rectangular prism surface area requires adding areas of all rectangular faces.
edge.failure_signal: Learner finds volume or only one pair of faces instead of total exposed area.

edge.rationale: Triangular prism surface area includes triangular faces whose areas must be calculated.
edge.failure_signal: Learner calculates rectangular faces but omits or miscalculates triangular faces.

edge.rationale: Composite solid surface area builds from surface area of simpler prisms and exposed-face reasoning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts hidden shared faces or omits exposed faces.

edge.rationale: Contextual surface-area problems require selecting exposed faces relevant to the context.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses volume when the context asks for covering material or surface coating.

edge.rationale: Contextual volume problems require selecting and applying an appropriate prism volume strategy.
edge.failure_signal: Learner calculates an area when a three-dimensional capacity or volume is needed.

edge.rationale: Solving missing dimensions requires rearranging a known prism volume relationship.
edge.failure_signal: Learner multiplies known dimensions again instead of using inverse operations.
